I don't really know much about menstrual cycles and I was wondering if women always use a tampon or pad or is it just during the final stage of menstruation (i.e. during your period).
AskWomen, do women have to use a tampon or pad all the time?

I hope you don't mind me giving you a bit more information than you asked for. I assure you that I don't mean for this to come across as condescending, but you did say you don't know much about menstrual cycles.

A woman's period isn't the "final stage of menstruation"; having a period actually marks the start of a woman's menstrual cycle. Menstruation is the period (pun fully intended) when a woman's body gets rid of the lining of her uterus, along with blood and other materials her uterus doesn't need. It does this (approximately) every lunar month when a woman isn't pregnant (i.e. her body expels it when it doesn't need to prepare to grow a fertilised egg). Women with a regular monthly cycle are generally at their most fertile on day 14 of their cycle.

Because of this, most women only use sanitary products when they're actually on their period. Some women wear pads or tampons (or sometimes both), and some women use a menstrual cup instead (personally, I'm a menstrual cup kinda girl). It can actually be pretty painful to use a tampon when you don't have your period (tampons are designed to soak up blood, so they soak up any other moisture in there too, making it very uncomfortable indeed).

Sometimes women wear pantyliners (extremely thin pads) for freshness on a day-to-day basis; some like to wear them when they're out for a long walk or at the gym. Some women just like being able to change their pantyliners several times a day to keep them feeling fresh. There are many different reasons why some women wear pantyliners every day, too (I'm not one of them though, so I can't give you my own opinion; sorry).

Everything I've said here is a very sweeping generalisation and, of course, every woman is different. For a variety of reasons (health reasons, contraceptives or other hormonal factors, other medications, etc.) some women don't have periods at all, or have very infrequent periods. Other women have regular cycles, but "regular" might mean "every 10 days", or it might mean "once every 10 weeks".

Sorry this is so long, but I wanted to give a comprehensive answer. If you have any further questions, please feel free to ask and I'll answer them as best as I can for you.

Thanks, I appreciate your honesty and I am glad you took the time to answer with all the extra info. It's really not something that is talked about much (probably because I'm a guy), but too much information is better than not knowing anything. :)
So in essence, a women is least fertile at the beginning of her period (immediately after the bleeding stops).

Yes, with the emphasis being on the word "least"; it's less likely that she'll get pregnant at that point in her cycle, but it's still possible. This is why some male/female couples think it's safe to have unprotected sex when the woman starts her period, because the chances of her getting pregnant are much lower.

In reality though, it's possible for a woman to get pregnant at any time during her menstrual cycle. Also, it's worth pointing out that, although ovulation (the most fertile period) usually happens around the midway point in a cycle (day 14), a woman never knows how long that specific cycle actually is while she's going through it (until her period arrives again, marking day one of the next cycle), so she has no idea if her cycle is 21 or 35 days long.

That said, many women who have a regular cycle can chart their fertile days with great precision and reliability (I used to to this myself when I was younger). No-one knows a woman's cycle better than that woman herself.
